title: Preference Modeling Diagnostics: Known-User Adaptation with Identity Controls

citation.apa: Guo, B. (2026). Preference modeling diagnostics: Known-user adaptation with identity controls [Frozen research artifact; CPU-only diagnostic study].
citation.chicago: Guo, Baixin. "Preference Modeling Diagnostics: Known-User Adaptation with Identity Controls." Frozen research artifact, 2026.
citation.mla: Guo, Baixin. Preference Modeling Diagnostics: Known-User Adaptation with Identity Controls. Frozen research artifact, 2026.

abstract: A frozen CPU-only diagnostic study that tests whether individual preference signal improves predictions on held-out prompts. It uses prompt-disjoint evaluation and wrong-user / shuffled-identity controls to separate stable signal from leakage. Regularized known-user adaptation reduced equal-user negative log-likelihood by 0.879% across 94 eligible users, while the controls removed the advantage. It is a research artifact, not a peer-reviewed publication.
